lines.text: Do you know how streaming works? The film isn't sent as one file. It's chopped into thousands of tiny pieces.
Each piece is just a few seconds of video, and every piece is stored at several qualities, from blurry to 4K.
Your player keeps measuring your internet speed, and picks the best quality it can download in time.
If your Wi-Fi slows down, the next piece arrives in lower quality. That's the blur you sometimes see, instead of a pause.
It also stays a few pieces ahead. That's the buffer, so a short hiccup never stops the show.
And the pieces come from servers close to you, copies of the film spread around the world.
Orbi moves big files in pieces too. Files up to twenty gigabytes go in parts of about thirty two megabytes, three at a time. If your connection drops, only the missing parts are sent again.
